summary: No static per-class starter spell pool exists. Spells are interactively selected by the player during character creation via a picker UI at wpcmk.ovr file offset 0x1ae9. Confirmed by: (1) ui_window_create call at 0x1b28, (2) stock characters TREON and PENTAG (both Mage) having different spellSlotsKnown contents in pcfile.dbs.

findings.claim: The spell-selection entry at wpcmk 0x1ae9 opens an interactive UI window (calls ui_window_create at wpcmk 0x1b28), proving spells are player-chosen, not statically assigned.

disassembly: e8 8b a0   ; call 0xbbb6   ; thunk to ui_window_create

findings.claim: Two Mage stock characters (TREON, PENTAG) have different spell contents, proving no static per-class starter pool.

evidence.conclusion: Different values for same class. Static table would produce identical values.

findings.claim: The school-init routine at wpcmk 0x3e51 initializes class rank thresholds (14 schools), NOT the specific spells known. It is not the starter-spell assignment.

evidence.notes: Documented in wpcmk-character-creation.md as 'Spell-school init at 0x3e51: 14 schools × per-class allocation. Matches the Wiz6 Realms architecture.' This sets rank thresholds (schoolRankThresholds at pcfile +0x152), not spell-known bits.

unresolved: The exact branch condition at wpcmk 0x1ae9 that gates the spell picker to spell-capable classes only — which class indices trigger the picker. The SPELL_PICKER_CLASSES set in starter-spells.ts (Mage/Priest/Alchemist/Bard/Psionic/Bishop) is inferred from the class design, not read from the branch bytes.

The exact encoding of the 20-byte spellSlotsKnown field at pcfile +0x188 — whether each byte is a count per school, a spell index, or something else. The field shows sparse nonzero values for casters but the per-byte semantics remain unresolved.
Whether the Bard class has a spell picker (Bards have a limited subset of spells; it's possible the picker branches differently for them).
